name: AEON
summary: My flagship system: a 240-module Python backend with a live React dashboard that ingests market data around the clock, runs a governed engine architecture, and turns raw data into plain-English briefings.
fullDescription: AEON is the system I've poured the most into. Underneath it is a 240-module Python backend (FastAPI + asyncio) running as production systemd services on Ubuntu, exposing 54 REST route modules to a live React operations dashboard — command center, analytics, regime performance, and alerts.

It's built for autonomy and safety: a central engine registry, an app-state singleton, a governance/kill-switch layer, and a self-healing watchdog with heartbeats. Async workers run on their own timers — market scans every few minutes, neural inference hourly, scheduled briefings. It stores ~900k documents in MongoDB and streams and scores Level 2 order-book data across exchanges.
The end goal I care about most is the 'understanding layer': taking all of that raw market data and turning it into clear, plain-English briefings I can actually reason from.
responsibilities: 240-module Python backend (FastAPI + asyncio) as production systemd services
54-module REST API feeding a real-time React dashboard
Engine registry, governance/kill-switch layer, and self-healing watchdog with heartbeats
~900k-document MongoDB store with real-time order-book ingestion and scoring
Async workers on independent timers plus plain-English research briefings

name: freeflow
summary: A private, on-device Windows voice-dictation app — local transcription with faster-whisper, optional Ollama cleanup, a global hotkey, native UI, and a packaged Windows installer.
fullDescription: freeflow is a shipped desktop product: a private, fully on-device voice-dictation app for Windows. Everything runs locally — faster-whisper handles transcription on-device, with optional Ollama-based text cleanup — so nothing has to leave your machine.

It has a global hotkey, a native UI, and a packaged Windows installer with proper release management. It's a complete, end-to-end product rather than a script: built in Python, packaged, and released.
responsibilities: On-device transcription with faster-whisper (no cloud dependency)
Optional local text cleanup via Ollama
Global hotkey and native Windows UI
Packaged Windows installer with release management

name: TOVAR Mobile Terminal
summary: A custom browser-based mobile terminal that lets me manage my production servers from my phone over a live tmux session.
fullDescription: TOVAR is a custom web terminal (Node.js + xterm.js, backed by tmux) that gives me full, comfortable control of my servers from a phone browser — scrollback, multiple windows, and touch-friendly controls.

It's also a good example of how I debug: a long-standing 'stuck output' bug that earlier attempts had blamed on CSS turned out to be a hardcoded tmux target deep in the server code. I traced it to the real root cause and fixed it properly.
responsibilities: Browser-based terminal with live tmux streaming and scrollback
Touch-friendly multi-window controls for mobile use
Root-caused and fixed a scroll bug that had defeated multiple prior attempts

name: F1 Event Parking Venture
summary: My own event-parking business for Formula 1 weekend — pricing strategy, online listings, and the logistics of running a 12-acre lot.
fullDescription: A venture I ran end to end: event parking for Formula 1 weekend. I set the pricing strategy, managed the online listings, and handled the on-the-ground logistics of operating a 12-acre lot during a high-demand event.
It's a small business but a real one — a compact example of spotting an opportunity, pricing it, marketing it, and executing the operations to deliver it.
responsibilities: Pricing strategy for a high-demand event
Logistics and operations for a 12-acre lot
